wanted: For the stray to tell me the real story of his scar and what the thing in the cistern was
For the 'twelve years ago' explained before it climbed out
For my name to turn out to be a mistake, a copy, something I could shed
feared: That the thing in the cistern was me - that the voice rising from the empty chamber was my own voice and I had already been lost, filed, or replaced twelve years ago and didn't know it
That the stray was lying about 'three minutes' and his fragment hadn't died but was waiting
attention_intensified: 032: the moment the stray parts the fur under his ruined ear and the 'scar' resolves into tiny letters that are not his name but mine - the whole scene was a countdown ('One.' 'Two.' 'Three.') and that reveal landed on the final slam of the paw on the lid
attention_weakened: 040d: the middle stretch where the orange light spills across the courtyard and replays Gistli Square beneath my feet - the replay mechanic (second-you, the jerk backward, the flinch) was already established in 000, so the second showing felt like re-watching rather than advancing; I was coasting until 'your name lengthens by one letter' and the rooftop silence re-locked me in
confused: 032: the cistern speaks in my voice ('He did not escape first.') and the stray immediately answers in his own ('He was sent first.') - it was unclear whether he was quoting the cistern, agreeing with it, or answering his own accusation

032: the dead sliver's 'three minutes' history sits oddly against the cistern's kit-like voice - I wasn't sure if the sliver and the climber were the same thing or two different remnants of the same event
residue: 'A fragment is not merely evidence that the Voyd exists. It is evidence against the cat who carried it.' - that stuck
The image of every rooftop cat falling silent at once, and the quiet dread that the city now knows which cat to ask next
I was left holding a name written under someone else's skin - mine - and a bell that had moved from beneath the city to above it
